solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pretentious report about urban areas in Israel and Bedfordshire

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the clue's place names are to be said out loud

parts.words: urban areas in Israel and Bedfordshire
parts.note: Haifa is a city in Israel and Luton a town in Bedfordshire

explanation.surface: A snooty write-up about a couple of towns, one in Israel and one in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Haifa Luton' quickly and it matches the word. Bedfordshire is an English county north of London; Luton is its biggest town.
explanation.definitionFit: Highfalutin is an informal adjective for pompous or showily grand, a close synonym of pretentious.

clue.text: Most religious stories are found in hotel bible section

parts.note: H is Hotel in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: things found in something sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, one section of the Bible
stories in the sense of untruths, fibs

explanation.surface: Fibs turn up in the scripture part of a hotel room, perhaps the Gideon Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy means devout or sacred, so the superlative describes whoever is most pious.

clue.text: Understand pent-up demand — too much pressure might cause it to blow

definitions.text: too much pressure might cause it to blow

indicators.note: pent-up means shut in, so the demand word is enclosed by the other word

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
to ask is to demand or request

explanation.surface: Suppressed demand, like steam, builds up until the excess pressure makes something burst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pent-up demand' reads as an economics phrase, but 'pent-up' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is an engine seal; excessive pressure makes it fail, giving the idiom 'blow a gasket'.

clue.text: Good reason for attraction

parts.note: fair means good, as in fair weather or a fair result
grounds are a reason or basis, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A sound justification for why someone is drawn to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair site with rides and stalls is a visitor attraction in the leisure sense.

clue.text: Ruddy cheek — fellow's wasted, drunk

indicators.note: wasted here means lost or thrown away, so the fellow letter is dropped

parts.note: a flush is the reddening of the cheeks

explanation.surface: A red-faced man who is completely wasted and drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' and 'drunk' look like a pair of synonyms describing the fellow; only 'drunk' is the definition, and 'wasted' signals the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is slang for a heavy drinker, a noun sense matching 'a drunk'.

clue.text: E.g. Jersey or Guernsey don't get a vote during cycle

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits inside the other
to cycle letters is to move one from the end round to the front

parts.note: if you don't get something you haven't got it, written without the apostrophe
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper as a vote

explanation.surface: Channel Islanders being denied the vote during some election cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' moves the final T of HAVENT to the front, giving THAVEN; 'during' then puts A and X inside it after the T. Jersey and Guernsey are the Channel Islands, self-governing islands off France with low taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both islands are well-known low-tax offshore financial centres, examples of such a place.

clue.text: Passage lost in initial Russian translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
initial picks out the opening letter of the word Russian

explanation.surface: A text extract that went missing in the first Russian version of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a piece of text tied to 'translation'; it is the definition, an airway.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is an air passage, an anatomical channel for breathing.

clue.text: More than one giant company gets little interest after depreciation

indicators.note: after places the little interest letter following the depreciation word

parts.note: depreciation is a loss of value
i is the short symbol for interest in finance

explanation.surface: A large firm earns a trickle of interest once its assets have been written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant company' looks like a big business; 'More than one giant' is the definition and 'company' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi is the plural of colossus, a huge statue or a person of enormous stature.

clue.text: Irregularly, a clear profit's taken in unofficial market

indicators.note: taken in means received inside, so one piece goes within the other
irregularly means in no set order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: boot is an old word for profit or advantage (as in 'to boot'), with the 's giving the S

explanation.surface: A trader makes an off-the-books net profit at some informal market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregularly' jumbles A CLEAR, and 'taken in' places the profit word inside. This is a British event where people sell junk from their car boots (trunks).
explanation.definitionFit: Such sales are informal gatherings of amateur sellers, a casual market rather than a licensed one.

clue.text: For former partners to eat out adds spice

indicators.note: out here means spread round the outside, so the eating word encloses the partners

parts.note: to sup is to eat, especially supper
exes are former spouses or partners

explanation.surface: Taking your ex-partners out for dinner livens things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sex something up is to make it more exciting or appealing, giving it extra zest.

clue.text: Losing current clout at EU, go bananas

parts.note: clout means power or influence

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country's influence in Brussels collapses as its diplomats go crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' clout, but it is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a cut in the electricity supply, so the flow of electricity is lost.

clue.text: Greek ruler travels west and east to mount comeback

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: emeer is a variant spelling of emir, a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A Greek leader tours the world, west then east, trying to return to power.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into view or public life after an absence is to make a return.

clue.text: Thin mark on top of compass?

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the other piece

parts.note: N, north, is at the top of a compass
an arrow is a mark pointing a direction

explanation.surface: The pointer mark at the top of a compass face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for one thing, the compass needle; the wordplay splits it into north plus a pointer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow and thin are synonyms describing something slender or of small width.

clue.text: Lack of progress for menfolk?

definitions.meaning: a state of standing still, with no growth or development
playfully, a whole nation of stags, stag being a term for men-only events

explanation.surface: Is the lack of progress the fault of men?
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British bachelor party, so 'stag' means men only.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic or social stillness, with nothing moving forward, is what standing water does.

clue.text: Exposes verbally: 'Oh, you tease!'

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the quoted words are said out loud

parts.note: the letters O, U and the word tease run together as speech

explanation.surface: Someone flirtatiously chides a person who has just revealed something.
explanation.definitionFit: To out someone is to reveal publicly a fact they kept secret, such as their sexuality.

clue.text: Aggressive dog mauling writer, let go in the end

indicators.note: mauling tears something apart, so these letters are mangled into a new order
in the end picks the final letter of the word go

explanation.surface: A savage dog attacks an author and only releases them at last.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a powerful German guard dog with a reputation for ferocity.

clue.text: Expression of exuberance and vitality? Hardly!

definitions.text: Expression of exuberance and vitality? Hardly!

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight
zing means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: Something is supposedly a display of high spirits and energy, but not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts spell out joy and vigour, while 'Hardly!' tells you the whole is the opposite: laboured, breathless breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasping, whistling breathing from asthma or illness is far from a sign of vigour.

clue.text: Don't hang around after physical contact — it's a bit iffy

definitions.text: Don't hang around after physical contact
definitions.meaning: read literally: make contact, then leave at once
uncertain or precarious, with the outcome in doubt

explanation.surface: Advice to leave straight after a touch, since the whole situation seems dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half describes the phrase literally, as in a pilot's landing and immediate take-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a risky situation whose outcome is uncertain until the last moment.

clue.text: Countless millions start to proliferate in limitless outer space

indicators.note: in places the millions and the starting letter inside the trimmed word
limitless strips the word outer of its boundary letters

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of proliferate

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide

explanation.surface: Vast numbers multiplying across the endless reaches of the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outer space' looks like one phrase, but 'limitless' trims only 'outer', and 'space' is a printer's term on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a great many, too many to count.

clue.text: List of prime numbers

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the word lies inside the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A mathematician's table of primes such as 2, 3, 5 and 7.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime numbers' points to maths; the answer straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare is a list of the dishes on offer.

clue.text: Upcoming book on setter's gut-wrenching

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above the following piece
in a down entry, upcoming means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tome is a large book
the setter refers to themself as I, so setter's is I've, I have

explanation.surface: A forthcoming book about the compiler is a harrowing read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming book' looks like a new release, but 'Upcoming' signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotive stirs strong feelings, as a harrowing story does.

clue.text: Worship a god appropriately therein

indicators.note: therein means within these words, so the answer sits in the run of letters

explanation.surface: A building where it is fitting to worship a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Worship' across 'a god' into 'appropriately', and the whole clue describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower temple in East Asia, a place of Buddhist worship.

clue.text: Fruit tea, they say, produced in Java?

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

indicators.note: they say indicates the word tea is heard, giving the sound of a letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like T

explanation.surface: A fruit-flavoured tea brewed on the island of Java.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Java' looks like the coffee island, but it is the programming language.
explanation.definitionFit: Applets are small programs, classically written in the Java programming language.

clue.text: A high shot, one hit on the turn, might describe this

definitions.text: A high shot, one hit on the turn, might describe this

indicators.note: on the turn means turning round, so the assembled pieces read backwards

parts.note: a lob is a high, arcing shot in tennis
a means one
rap means hit or strike

explanation.surface: A tennis lob, struck as the ball turns, traces a curve through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces A, LOB, A, RAP are read backwards together; the whole clue describes the curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile's path under gravity is the curve mathematicians name after the conic section.

clue.text: Having skill shortage with no French here

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the French word is removed

parts.note: a deficit is a shortage
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A skills shortage in which no French speakers are available locally.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means neatly skilful, especially with the hands.

clue.text: Back in bygone time, recluse

indicators.note: in places the reversed time word within the old word for before

parts.note: ere is an archaic word meaning before, of time gone by

indicators.note: back means the word time is read in reverse

parts.note: the word time itself

explanation.surface: A hermit returns to the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in bygone time' reads as one phrase about the past; 'Back' reverses only 'time', and 'in' puts that inside the bygone word.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit, one living alone in seclusion.

clue.text: View through rose-tinted spectacles to pick up cases of lazy eye

indicators.note: to pick up is to hear, as a radio picks up a signal

parts.note: idle eyes, more than one instance of a lazy eye

explanation.surface: An optician hands out rose-tinted glasses to treat a lazy eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' and 'lazy eye' build an optician's scene; 'View through rose-tinted spectacles' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To see someone through rose-tinted glasses is to view them uncritically, to adore them.

clue.text: Evening watching TV, perhaps, with good beer and bird

parts.note: a night in is an evening spent at home, perhaps in front of the television
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A cosy evening of television, a pint, and some birdwatching.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a small songbird famous for singing at night.
